'''Étienne Georges Alfred Roth ''' (born 5 June 1922 in Strasbourg, died 19 March 2009 in Sèvres) was a French nuclear chemist, son of Professor George Roth and Marguerite Neymarck.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.whoswho.fr/decede/biographie-etienne-roth_12567|title=Etienne Roth - Who's who in France}}</ref>

From 1980-87 Roth served as the Director of Research for the separations and isotopic studies of Physical Chemistry Division (1980–87) at the [[Commissariat à l'énergie atomique et aux énergies alternatives|Atomic Energy and Alternative Energies Commission]]. During his scientific career he was a visiting Scientist at US Brookhaven National Laboratory (1957-1958), Chairman of the [[Commission on Isotopic Abundances and Atomic Weights|Atomic Weights Commission]] (1976-1979). In his career, Roth has authored more than one hundred and fifty scientific articles and several books on applied nuclear chemistry, and has invented several methods for industrial separation of isotopes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lactualitechimique.org/larevue_article.php?cle=2173|title=Etienne Roth (1922-2009)|journal=L'Actualité Chimique|date=June 2009|pages=63–64}}</ref>

The Prix Étienne Roth was established in his honour.<ref>[http://www.upmc.fr/fr/recherche/talents_et_decouvertes/prix_et_distinctions/2004/jerome_gaillardet_laureat_2004_prix_etienne_roth_du_cea.html Jérôme Gaillardet, lauréat 2004 Prix Étienne Roth du CEA] Jérôme Gaillardet, professeur à l’Institut de physique du globe (UMR 7154) reçoit le Prix Étienne Roth du Commissariat à l’énergie atomique pour l’année 2004.</ref>
